captions.detailed: This 3D-printable model features a rectangular box with rounded vertical corners and a separate flat lid. One of the long vertical faces of the box is perforated with an evenly spaced grid of eight circular holes, arranged in two rows of four. The upper rim of the box has a small rectangular notch cut out of the center of its two shorter walls, corresponding to a central alignment rib running across the top face of the lid.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric electronic project box with a separate lid in OpenSCAD. The box should have rounded corners, a customizable grid of circular jack-mounting holes on one face, and a central alignment notch/beam system to ensure the lid fits securely.
captions.factory: The box is created using a minkowski sum of a cylinder and a cube to get rounded outer corners, which is then hollowed out with a smaller cube. A nested for-loop distributes cylindrical cutouts along the front face based on the calculated inter-hole spacing. A large cube cuts off the top of the box to create the open container, and a small cube cuts a notch across the top rim. The lid is generated in a union block using a minkowski sum of a cylinder and a flat cube, with a matching alignment beam cube added on top.
